Customer (Amanda Scott): There's a gas smell in the kitchen and it's getting stronger.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Hi Amanda Scott, Karabo Zulu here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Amanda Scott): Is it safe for me to stay in the house right now?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): You did the right thing calling. Let's get you safe first.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Are you and everyone else out of the house now? What's the address?
Customer (Amanda Scott): We're outside now, on the front lawn. It's the house on the corner.
Customer (Amanda Scott): How long until someone actually gets here?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Did you switch anything on or off before you left?
Customer (Amanda Scott): No, we just walked out.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Is anyone in the house who couldn't get out?
Customer (Amanda Scott): No, everyone's out, the dog too.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Is there a phone number the technician can reach you on?

Agent (Karabo Zulu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): A technician is being sent now. Gas odour calls go straight to the front of the queue.
Customer (Amanda Scott): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): A technician is on the way and should be there within 30 minutes — in the meantime, don't use any switches or open flames, and I'll call you back the moment they're on site.
Customer (Amanda Scott): What will they do when they get here?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Check the house and meter for leaks and make it safe. They won't leave until it is.
Customer (Amanda Scott): Should we call the fire department?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): If the smell gets stronger or you hear a loud hiss, yes, call 911 as well.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): To recap: the technician is on the way, stay outside, and don't use switches or flames until they've checked it.
Customer (Amanda Scott): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
